html:
Overnight working model — 2026-09-13 (until 08:00 PDT)

Companion to the brief docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-13-hosted-pipeline-brief.md (binding on what). This document is binding on how: roles, design bar, frozen interfaces, streams, cadence, verification. The integrator follows it; every stream brief links to it.

1. Roles

  • Integrator (this session, fable): freezes interfaces, dispatches streams, merges, runs contract tests, deploys, rules on conflicts, keeps the ledger (.superpowers/sdd/2026-09-13-hosted-pipeline/progress.md) and pushes main.
  • Stream implementers (fable, one per stream, own worktree, disjoint file ownership, no subagents of their own): implement from a brief file, tests first for every contract, commit on their branch, write a report file, return status + commits + one-line test summary + concerns.
  • Stream reviewers (fable): a task review per stream report (spec compliance + code quality against §2), then one whole-branch review before the final push.
  • Recon and mechanical helpers (opus/sonnet): reading docs, collecting evidence, formatting, running documented commands. Never haiku.
  • Operator stream (fable, later in the night): submits the creation and run workflows through the console and the CLI, watches the funnel and spend, tunes bands and concurrency from data, records everything in the ledger.

Parallelism is the point: streams run concurrently in worktrees; the integrator never implements a stream itself while streams are running, it integrates. Dispatch prompts carry only the stream brief path, the frozen interfaces, the global constraints and the report path; never the session history.

2. Design bar (what "well designed" means here)

Code. Minimal is not the requirement; correct, clear and durable is.

  • One responsibility per module; module docstrings state the contract; public functions have typed signatures and short docstrings that say what is guaranteed, not what the code does.
  • Errors are classified at the boundary: invalid input and business rejections raise typed, non-retryable errors; transient failures propagate as retryable; nothing is swallowed. Every except names a type and a reason.
  • No hidden state: configuration enters through typed settings objects built from the environment once; no module reads os.environ in the middle of a function.
  • Idempotency by construction: every activity can run twice; every write is write-then-rename or an upsert keyed by id.
  • Tests before implementation for every contract in the interfaces spec; tests assert behaviour, not strings.
  • No cleverness that a reviewer would need explained; a comment answers "why", never "what".

Data models. Every entity has exactly one Pydantic model (strict, extra="forbid"), one Postgres table, one bucket location, and they agree field for field.

  • Ids: content-addressed where the artifact is immutable (spec hash, compiled hash, trial id), ULIDs where it is not (workflows already have Temporal ids). Versions are explicit integers, never implied by timestamps.
  • Every row carries provenance: created_at, updated_at, workflow_id, run_id, worker_image_digest, origin.
  • Nullable means "unknown", never "false" or "not applicable"; enums are enums; money is numeric(12,6) USD; times are UTC timestamptz.
  • Migrations are forward-only Alembic revisions; the index is rebuildable from the bucket, so a bad migration is fixed by a new revision plus a rebuild, never by editing data by hand.
  • The bucket layout is part of the data model (brief §2.3): paths are derived by one function, never assembled ad hoc.

Decisions. Every non-obvious choice is written down where it is made: a Ruling: line in the ledger (what, why, cost if wrong) for the integrator, a decisions section in each stream report for implementers. The right decision is the one that keeps the record honest and the reward trustworthy, then the one that keeps the operator's surface simple, then the one that is cheapest.

3. Phase 0 — freeze the interfaces (integrator, first 45 minutes)

Published as code stubs with tests plus docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-13-interfaces.md; streams start only after this commit is on main:

  1. swesim/storage/layout.py — the bucket layout (brief §2.3) as one Layout class: scenario_dir(id, version), task_dir(id, version, condition), trial_dir(trial_id), export_path, candidates_dir(source_key, date), evidence_dir(kind, date), calibration_dir(judge, date); Workspace becomes a thin adapter over it. Tests pin every path string.
  2. swesim/index/models.py + swesim/index/schema.py — Pydantic rows and SQLAlchemy tables for scenarios, candidates, trials, exchanges, scores, workflows, costs, operator_actions; swesim/index/store.py with upsert_* and rebuild_from_layout(); Alembic initialised.
  3. swesim/workflows/launchers/base.py — the launcher protocol (launch_once, read_evidence, decide_launch, cancel) with the systemd implementation moved behind it unchanged; cloudrun.py is a stream deliverable.
  4. swesim/workflows/queues.py — queue names and the activity→queue map; swesim/workflows/retries.py — retry classes.
  5. swesim/workflows/search_attributes.py — the six keys and the setter used at every workflow start.
  6. swesim/costs.py — CostRecord and the provider price table with a price_source field.
  7. swesim/dashboard/data.py — the console's data-access interface (functions returning the Pydantic rows above), implemented first over the files, then over Postgres by the storage stream; the console stream codes against it.
  8. swesim/settings.py — one typed Settings (env file path, bucket, database URL, Temporal, IAP evaluators, spend cap), replacing scattered os.environ reads.

4. Streams (parallel worktrees; owner files disjoint)

Stream Owns Depends on Deliverable check
infra infra/**, scripts/cloud/**, Makefile cloud targets — terraform apply twice, second clean; outputs file
image+deploy Dockerfile.worker, cloudbuild.yaml, infra/run/**, deploy target infra outputs pools + console deployed at a digest; verify_cloud.sh
launcher+temporal swesim/workflows/launchers/cloudrun.py, queue routing in workflows.py/activities.py, retries, patched, continue-as-new, cancellation, split of mine/validate Phase 0 unit tests with fake Cloud Run API; restart proof on the deployed stack
storage+index swesim/storage/**, swesim/index/**, swesim/paths.py adapter, scripts/cloud/import_vm.sh, swesim index CLI Phase 0 rebuild from bucket equals files; import of the VM record labelled
console swesim/dashboard/** (UI/UX per brief §2.5 and §2.5.1: history, browsers, actions, leaderboard, design system) Phase 0 data interface screenshots both modes; IAP gate test; no evaluator leak test
review-fixes swesim/stakeholder/**, swesim/stages/draft_spec.py, swesim/sources/github_repo.py (probe reuse), swesim/stages/score.py grouping — tests per Codex row (brief §7.1)
models swesim/llm.py, swesim/stages/run.py provider table, OpenRouter in the solver path, judge/stakeholder switch, calibration with per-instance predictions — probe file; one OpenRouter smoke trial
task-sense swesim/audit/** (rubric, LLM-assisted transcript audit, question-quality and disclosure-timing labels, report) trial records report on all v2 transcripts; labels in the index
docs docs/setup.md, docs/runbook.md, README quickstart, .env.example, architecture/ops/grading updates everything, late fresh-clone run recorded
operator ledger, sweep submissions, tuning smoke passed funnel and leaderboard live

Conflicts are avoided by ownership; a stream that needs a change in another stream's file asks the integrator, who rules and either edits main or reassigns.

5. Cadence and integration

  • Streams report at 30-minute checkpoints (a line in their report file); the integrator reconciles live streams every checkpoint and chases silent ones.
  • Merge rule: a stream merges when its own tests pass, the contract suite passes on the merged tree, and its task review is clean or its findings are ruled on. main is never red; every merge is pushed.
  • Deploy rule: any merge touching worker or console code deploys to Cloud Run through make deploy after the open-executions check; the digest is recorded in the ledger.
  • Fix loops: up to three resumes of the same implementer, then a fresh implementer; never more than five rounds; parked findings are ruled on in the ledger.

6. Timeline (PDT)

Time Milestone
01:15 Phase 0 interfaces on main; streams dispatched
01:15–03:30 Round 1: infra applied; image built; launcher + queues; storage + index; console skeleton over files; review fixes; OpenRouter
03:30–04:00 Integration 1; smoke create + run on the new stack; console cutover behind IAP
04:00–05:30 Creation sweep (repositories first); round 2: console pages, task-sense audit, docs drafts
05:30–07:00 Difficulty screen; Tier A–C runs; leaderboard live; Codex-row fixes verified in the sweep
07:00–08:00 Final whole-branch review, verify scripts, docs with measured numbers, ledger, push

If the smoke on the new stack has not passed by 04:00, the integrator rules on the fallback (brief §8) and records it.

7. Task sense, disclosure timing and question quality (the audit that gates the leaderboard)

A leaderboard is only as good as its tasks. The task-sense stream builds and runs an audit over every scenario and every interactive transcript, evaluator-only, LLM-assisted with claude-opus-5, with a rubric and per-item labels stored in the index and summarised in docs/grading.md:

  • Does the task make sense? The natural brief plus the stakeholder-visible facts must be a coherent ask; every hidden test must be a fair consequence of the brief and the facts, not of the oracle's incidental choices; withheld spans must be things a reporter would plausibly omit and a developer would plausibly ask about. Labels: coherent, fair-tests, plausible-withholding, each with a reason.
  • Does the stakeholder reveal the right information at the right time? For each reply: was the disclosed fact targeted by the question (not volunteered), was anything test-derived or identifier-level disclosed, did a confirmation stay at behaviour level, was patience spent sensibly. Labels per reply; counts per model and per scenario.
  • Are the agents asking the right questions? For each question: specific and decision-oriented, asked before the relevant implementation, not fishing, not redundant with the brief. Labels per question; the interaction metrics (asked-before-implementing rate, questions per trial, useful-question rate) join the leaderboard as columns.
  • Reward hacking signals (brief §7) are joined per trial; any trial with a signal is listed under the model's row.

Findings feed back the same night into the drafter prompt (withholding selection), the stakeholder prompt, the judge's gap criteria, and the difficulty labels. Nothing on the leaderboard skips this audit.

8. Verification and honesty

  • No claim without the command and its output; evidence files under the bucket's evidence/ prefix and referenced by path.
  • The offline suite, the contract suite, verify.sh 10 and verify_cloud.sh run before the final push; failures are reported as failures.
  • Numbers in docs come from the index at the time of writing, with the query or script that produced them.
  • Secrets never enter prompts, reports, logs, payloads or git.
